constraint: Closely spaced parallel runways (centerlines ~750 ft apart). Side-by-side approaches were ended by the FAA on 2026-03-30; staggered approaches (from 2026-08-12) allow up to ~42 arrivals/hour, versus ~54 previously, and ~30–36 in low visibility.
impact: Arrival capacity, not passenger demand, is the binding constraint. Demand that cannot be scheduled shows up as high load factors, NAS delays and ground delay programs.

constraint: John Wayne Airport Settlement Agreement (amended 2014): passenger cap of 11.8 million annual passengers from 2021, possibly up to 12.5M from 2026; a limit on daily commercial departures; and a nighttime curfew (no scheduled departures 10pm–7am) through 2035.
impact: Growth is capped by regulation, not by infrastructure. Terminal expansion alone cannot add flights while the agreement stands.
New flights require slots, so terminal investment does not translate directly into more flights.

constraint: Operations limited by FAA Order (equivalent to Level 3 slot control).
impact: Flight growth is capped administratively, so additional demand appears as higher fares and load factors.

constraint: Operations limited by FAA High Density Rule slots (equivalent to Level 3 slot control).
impact: Flight growth is capped administratively, so additional demand appears as higher fares and load factors.
